title: BJP holds Loktantra Bachao march in Bhopal led by JP Nadda

tea.why: To counter the Congress party and opposition criticism of the Election Commission and electronic voting machines.
tea.want: To defend constitutional institutions and protest against opposition attempts to create instability.
tea.changed: Nov 4: BJP leaders led a foot march from Atal Path to Roshanpura Square in Bhopal.

summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) organised a foot march in Bhopal under the banner of 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy). Union Minister JP Nadda, Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, and state BJP president Hemant Khandelwal led the procession from Atal Path to Roshanpura Square, passing through areas like New Market. Thousands of participants, including party workers, traders, doctors, lawyers, and members of various social organisations, joined the demonstration. Speakers accused the Congress party and the opposition INDIA bloc of spreading anarchy, undermining democratic institutions, and fostering public distrust in the Election Commission following electoral defeats. The march formed part of a statewide counter-campaign launched by the BJP in response to opposition protests regarding electoral rolls and voting procedures.
demands: Protect constitutional institutions from opposition attacks
End opposition criticism of the Election Commission
response: No government crackdown or adverse police response was reported, as the event was a ruling party-backed march.

updates.text: Union Minister JP Nadda and Chief Minister Mohan Yadav led the Loktantra Bachao march in Bhopal.
